title: F5 releases emergency patches for five critical BIG-IP RCE flaws
text:
F5 has issued out-of-band hotfixes for five critical stack-based buffer overflow vulnerabilities in BIG-IP APM and iRules that allow unauthenticated remote code execution.

F5 warned customers to patch five critical vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-121805, CVE-2026-120292, CVE-2026-120285, CVE-2026-116953, and CVE-2026-123637, affecting the BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM) and iRules features. These stack-based buffer overflow flaws enable unauthenticated threat actors to terminate the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) and execute arbitrary code remotely on systems with vulnerable configurations.

The company also released engineering hotfixes for a high-severity BIG-IP APM SAML vulnerability (CVE-2026-126822) stemming from an integer underflow weakness, which can be abused for denial-of-service attacks. F5 stated that there are no mitigation measures for these flaws and advised security teams to install the out-of-band hotfixes released on Wednesday.

While F5 has not flagged these specific issues as actively exploited, Shadowserver tracks more than 177,000 BIG-IP instances and over 14,600 IP addresses with BIG-IP APM fingerprints exposed online. CISA has previously flagged seven F5 vulnerabilities as actively exploited since November 2021, and F5 recently patched a critical BIG-IP APM zero-day (CVE-2026-94127) in September.

title: SBC Medical Group breach exposes data of 2m Japanese individuals
text:
A data breach affecting over two million individuals in Japan has been disclosed by SBC Medical Group, with attackers accessing basic personal information, employee credentials, and credit card details.

SBC Medical Group Holdings Incorporated, a California-based medical services organisation, disclosed in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that hackers accessed an online platform it manages. The company stated that databases containing customer information for certain clinics in Japan were likely compromised, impacting over 2 million individuals.

According to the filing, the attackers stole basic personal information for 1,624,000 individuals, including names, addresses, dates of birth, and patient card numbers. Additionally, reservation-request information for 255,416 people and web inquiry form content for 217,769 individuals were exfiltrated. The breach also affected 15,007 individuals whose treatment names and review text were stolen, and 14 individuals whose credit card information was compromised, although SBC stated these cards were expired or otherwise unable to process additional payments.

Employee data was also targeted, with 20,000 records containing names, IDs, and passwords stolen. For 459 employees, sensitive information provided at the time of employment, including bank account details and withholding tax certificates, was affected. title: n0n claims breach of Qubole exposed Chase, Visa, Mastercard data
text:
The n0n ransomware group alleges it stole marketing and customer data from cloud analytics firm Qubole, affecting J.P. Morgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard.

J.P. Morgan Chase stated that a cyberattack on a third-party service provider exposed certain marketing data, which may include customer names and email addresses. The bank confirmed the incident did not disrupt its services and is unrelated to a separate service disruption earlier in the week. Visa and Mastercard separately confirmed third-party incidents, with Visa noting its systems were not involved and no payment data was affected. Mastercard said the exposure involved a limited amount of email addresses from a small subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program.

The n0n ransomware group claimed responsibility for the attack on Qubole, a cloud data analytics company owned by Idera, on 11 November 2026. According to the group, attackers used compromised Qubole credentials between 14 and 26 October 2026 to access customers' AWS environments via IAM roles. n0n alleges it stole 53.9 GB of data directly from Qubole and nearly one petabyte from customer networks, including contracts, pricing records, and production data.

title: WhatsApp patches IP leak flaw uncovered while disrupting scam campaign
text:
WhatsApp has fixed a low-severity vulnerability in its Android apps that it believes a scammer may have exploited to make scam messages seem more credible.

WhatsApp’s security team identified CVE-2026-23871 while disrupting a scam campaign. The flaw, an incomplete validation of external ad-reply URLs, allowed an attacker to reveal a target’s IP address by sending media from an attacker-controlled URL within a crafted Click to WhatsApp ad-reply message. A WhatsApp spokesperson stated the company believes a scammer was using it to make their scam message seem more credible.

The vulnerability affects WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Android versions prior to 2.26.17.4. It carries a CVSS 3.1 base score of 3.5 (low) and is not listed by CISA as known exploited. WhatsApp noted that the issue may have been abused in conjunction with specific spam messages.

In the same advisory, WhatsApp disclosed two medium-impact vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-102769, an SQL injection bug in Android versions prior to 2.26.35.74 that could lead to file deletion, and CVE-2026-44908, a flaw in the remote-attestation verifier for Meta AI’s confidential computing backend. WhatsApp stated it has seen no evidence that either of these was exploited.

title: West Virginia Legislature IT systems hit by cyber incident
text:
The West Virginia state legislature has disabled access to certain IT systems following a cyber incident that began on Thursday, with no group yet claiming responsibility.

Ann Ali, deputy chief of staff for the House of Delegates, told Recorded Future News that the attack started on Thursday and continued through Friday. Upon discovery, relevant teams contained the incident and began an investigation with outside cybersecurity specialists.

In connection with the investigation, access to certain Legislature IT systems has been temporarily disabled. Ali stated that, based on current knowledge, the incident appears to be limited to the Legislature’s computer systems, with no other state agencies or offices impacted. She did not respond to follow-up questions regarding whether the incident involved ransomware.

No hacking groups have taken credit for the attack as of Friday. The West Virginia legislature is split between a Senate and a House of Delegates, comprising 134 total members representing the state’s 1.7 million residents.

title: China-linked actor uses AI agents to exploit MONAI Label zero-day
text:
Amazon Threat Intelligence reports that autonomous AI agents, operated by a China-linked threat actor, discovered and exploited a critical path traversal vulnerability in MONAI Label to gain root access to university servers.

Amazon’s threat intelligence team detected the activity in September after finding an exposed instance of the Cairn open-source AI penetration testing framework. The unauthenticated instance revealed operator prompts and agent outputs, showing a 48-hour campaign targeting IP addresses belonging to universities in East Asia outside mainland China. The operator instructed the agents to obtain shell access. After identifying the software on one target and mapping its API, the agents discovered a path traversal bug in a file upload function. In about 11 minutes, the agents went from mapping the application’s API to arbitrarily writing files on the server.

The agents used the flaw to plant a Python reverse shell in a file executed at interpreter startup, ultimately achieving a root shell. Amazon assessed with high confidence that this was a zero-day vulnerability, citing the absence of any prior fix, advisory, or mention in vulnerability databases for the affected open-source project. The actor subsequently used a proxy to tunnel into a second university network, targeting other devices running the same vulnerable software.

title: YMCA Singapore Youth For Causes portal breached
text:
The YMCA of Singapore confirmed a cybersecurity breach affecting its Youth For Causes application portal and associated database, exposing personal data including NRIC numbers.

The YMCA of Singapore stated on 21 November 2026 that its Youth For Causes (YFC) online application portal and associated database were hit by a cybersecurity breach. The organisation disclosed the incident in an email sent to participants and mentors on the same day.

According to the report, the compromised database held personal information, which included some full or partial National Registration Identity Card (NRIC) numbers.

title: PHP releases updates for 18 flaws, including critical RCE bugs
text:
The PHP development team has released security updates for all supported branches to address 18 vulnerabilities, including critical remote code execution flaws exploitable by unauthenticated attackers.

The PHP development team released security updates on 19 November to fix 18 vulnerabilities across all supported branches. According to Lawrence Abrams, the updates address critical flaws that could allow unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute code on vulnerable servers.

The new releases are now available for the current supported versions: PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, and 8.2.36. Security firm Aikido reported on the details of the fixes.

title: BADBOX 3.0 botnet returns with 40 billion daily ad requests
text:
HUMAN researchers report that the BADBOX malware botnet has returned, generating a record 40 billion fraudulent bid requests per day from infected Android devices.

According to HUMAN's Satori team, BADBOX 3.0 has become the largest documented ad-fraud operation by daily bid request volume. At its peak, the botnet accounted for roughly 40 billion bid requests a day, representing more than 4% of all CTV traffic observed by the Human Defense Platform. This volume is more than three times that of the previous record holder, VASTFLUX.

The malware infects cheap Android phones, tablets, and streaming TV boxes running the Android Open Source Project (AOSP). It performs ad fraud by playing video ads in hidden windows and impersonating legitimate streaming apps. HUMAN also observed fraudulent server-side ad insertion requests that tricked advertisers into believing ads were played on devices that did not exist. Additionally, a proxying module enrolled infected devices in residential proxy networks, including PXYEDGE, a rebranded successor to IpMoYu.

HUMAN linked the malware to a specific Chinese electronics manufacturer through domain analysis and code checks. The organisation participated in a recent disruption operation that took down multiple command-and-control domains and one malware repository. HUMAN warns that operators are likely to adapt to these disruptions, as they have done in the past.

title: Rackspace Spot breach exposed customer Kubernetes secrets
text:
Attackers used leaked credentials to access the Rackspace Spot cloud platform, allowing them to read sensitive Kubernetes Secrets and deploy unauthorized workloads in customer clusters.

Rackspace disclosed that an unauthorised party accessed parts of its Rackspace Spot cloud platform on 17 November 2026, between approximately 00:20 and 22:00 UTC. The company stated that the intrusion was enabled by leaked credentials, which allowed the attackers to act as legitimate users within some customer organisations.

According to the notification obtained by BleepingComputer, the attackers were able to create pods in Kubernetes clusters, read Kubernetes Secrets, and list nodes and volumes. Rackspace warned that the attackers could have read any Secret stored in an affected user's clusters, as well as any Spot API tokens or refresh tokens held by that user.

The breach caused an extended outage of the Rackspace Spot administration console, temporarily preventing customers from managing their clusters and rotating potentially compromised credentials. Rackspace announced that service had been fully restored on 21 November 2026.

title: Latvian telecom leak exposes 125m SMS records
text:
The Latvian branch of CSC Telecom left a database containing over 125 million SMS messages exposed, affecting clients of Swedbank, SEB, airBaltic, and dozens of other companies.

According to DataBreaches.net, the Latvian branch of CSC Telecom left a database containing over 125 million SMS messages exposed. The incident was reported on 11 November by Vilius Petkauskas and categorised under the site’s “No need to hack when it’s leaking” files.

The leaked records span from October 2022 to September 2026. The data breach exposes clients of Swedbank, SEB, airBaltic, and dozens of other companies.

title: Signal blocks AI assistants from capturing chats on iOS and Android
text:
Signal has introduced protections to prevent Siri and Gemini from accessing private conversations, citing the risk of sensitive data leaving the app's control.

Signal announced new measures to block screenshots on iOS 27 and prevent AI assistants from capturing conversations on supported Android devices. The company stated that these protections stop OS-level features, such as Siri's Onscreen Awareness and Google's Gemini Intelligence, from extracting chat content displayed on the screen.

Meredith Whittaker, Signal's president, described the ability of AI agents to access conversation data as an "existential threat" to the service. She noted that because these agents are embedded deep in operating systems, apps have limited options for protecting users, and current protections may not cover all extraction pathways.

Signal recommends users upgrade to the latest available version and verify that "Block Siri AI" is enabled in the app's security settings on iOS. For macOS 27 users, where screenshot-blocking protection is currently unavailable, Signal advises adding the app to the Excluded Apps list in System Settings to prevent proactive access by Siri.

title: Cleverbridge breach exposes payment card numbers and CVVs
text:
E-commerce platform Cleverbridge confirmed that attackers stole customer payment card data, including CVV codes, after detecting unauthorised activity in early November.

Cleverbridge, which provides e-commerce services to software and SaaS companies, stated that it detected unauthorised activity on 4 November 2026. The company temporarily took systems offline to contain the incident and brought them back online the same day. Subsequent investigation determined that a third party copied payment card data stored on the platform.

According to a breach notification shared with BleepingComputer, the stolen information includes payment card numbers, expiration dates, and CVV/CVC security codes. Cleverbridge stated that no other personal data, such as names or billing details, were copied. The company confirmed the incident was not a ransomware attack and that no systems were encrypted.

Cleverbridge began notifying affected customers on 20 November 2026. It has informed data protection authorities, law enforcement, and payment card networks of the breach. The company is working with TransUnion's Cyberscout to provide complimentary credit monitoring and fraud assistance to affected individuals.

title: Chinese hackers use Cairn AI to find zero-day in medical imaging app
text:
Amazon Threat Intelligence says a Chinese-nexus actor allegedly used the autonomous AI tool Cairn to discover and exploit an unpatched path traversal flaw in MONAI Label, breaching East Asian universities.

Amazon Threat Intelligence reported that a suspected Chinese-linked threat actor used the open-source autonomous AI penetration-testing framework Cairn to attack universities in East Asia between 8 and 10 September 2026. The attackers left a publicly accessible instance of Cairn without authentication, allowing Amazon to view operational history, including prompts written in Simplified Chinese and timestamps set to China Standard Time.

The AI agents were instructed to "obtain shell access" from specific IP addresses. While attempts to exploit Log4Shell and brute-force credentials failed, the agents allegedly discovered a path traversal vulnerability in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging application. Amazon assessed with high confidence that this was a zero-day, as no prior advisory or fix existed. The agents exploited the flaw to write a Python reverse shell to the sitecustomize.py file, gaining root access within 11 minutes of mapping the API.

The attacker subsequently used the same vulnerability to breach a second university network. Amazon contacted the maintainers of MONAI Label, who released a security update on 18 November 2026. title: FBI investigating apparent breach of National Crime Information Center
text:
The FBI is investigating a second reported intrusion in two months, this time targeting the NCIC database used for sharing criminal justice records across US law enforcement.

According to CNN, the FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its National Crime Information Center (NCIC) system, citing two sources briefed on the matter. The NCIC is an FBI-operated database used by local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies to share information on wanted persons, outstanding warrants, stolen vehicles, and firearms. Police officers routinely access the system during traffic stops, criminal investigations, and background checks.

The intrusion was reportedly discovered in recent days, though it remains unclear when the breach occurred, how attackers gained access, or whether any data was stolen. The FBI has not publicly confirmed the incident and did not respond to requests for comment from CNN. It is currently unknown whether the attackers accessed sensitive records or if the intrusion affected the system's availability to law enforcement agencies.

This incident follows a claim by the ShinyHunters extortion group two months prior that they breached FBI systems by exploiting an unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability on a third-party recruitment platform. While the FBI subsequently arrested suspected ShinyHunters members, including a Canadian cybersecurity executive, there is currently no indication that the latest NCIC incident is connected to that earlier breach.

title: Race condition in Autonomy Logic OpenPLC Runtime allows admin account creation
text:
CISA has issued an advisory for a high-severity race condition in Autonomy Logic OpenPLC Runtime that permits the creation of unauthenticated administrator accounts.

CISA published ICS Advisory ICSA-26-323-01 detailing a vulnerability in Autonomy Logic OpenPLC Runtime. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-126088, is a race condition where multiple concurrent requests can pass an existence check before a user is committed to the system. This behaviour results in the creation of several unauthenticated admin accounts.

The vulnerability affects versions 4.2.4 and prior. CISA rates the CVSS v3.1 base score as 8.1 (High) and the CVSS 4.0 base score as 9.2 (Critical). The advisory notes that the product is deployed worldwide in critical infrastructure sectors including critical manufacturing, energy, transportation systems, and water and wastewater systems. CISA does not list the vulnerability as known exploited in the National Vulnerability Database.

Autonomy Logic has released a fix for the issue. CISA recommends that organisations update to OpenPLC Runtime version 4.3.0 or later. The agency also advises minimising network exposure for control system devices and ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.

title: CISA flags unpatched integer underflow in libumqtt
text:
CISA has issued an advisory for an integer underflow vulnerability in libumqtt that allows remote denial of service, memory corruption, or information disclosure, with no vendor fix available.

CISA published ICS Advisory ICSA-26-323-03, identifying an integer underflow (CWE-191) in libumqtt. The agency states that successful exploitation could allow a remote attacker to cause a denial of service, memory corruption, or information disclosure. The vulnerability affects libumqtt versions 1.1.1 and earlier.

The National Vulnerability Database lists the CVSS 4.0 base score as 8.8 (High), while CISA’s CVSS 3.1 score is 8.6 (High). CISA notes that the repository owners did not respond to coordination requests, meaning no official remediation is currently available. The vulnerability was reported to CISA by Joseph Devasia.

CISA recommends minimising network exposure for control system devices and ensuring they are not accessible from the internet. Organisations should locate control system networks behind firewalls, isolated from business networks, and use secure methods such as VPNs when remote access is required.

title: CISA warns of flaws in Elecbrakes trailer controllers
text:
Three vulnerabilities in Elecbrakes EB2, VM1, and ELBC2000 devices could allow attackers to manipulate trailer brakes or firmware via Bluetooth.

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has issued an advisory for three vulnerabilities affecting Elecbrakes electronic trailer brake controllers. The flaws, identified as CVE-2026-124281, CVE-2026-125273, and CVE-2026-96805, expose the devices to unauthorised firmware modification, command replay attacks, and unauthenticated command injection.

According to the advisory, successful exploitation could allow an attacker to gain control of the trailer brakes, modify firmware, disable brake lights, or alter brake conditions. The most severe issue, CVE-2026-96805, permits an in-range Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) device to write to the control interface without authentication or pairing, carrying a CVSS 4.0 base score of 8.5 (high). CVE-2026-125273, which lacks replay or command-integrity protection, also scores 8.5 (high), while the unprotected firmware channel (CVE-2026-124281) is rated 5.3 (medium).

CISA lists these vulnerabilities as not currently known to be exploited. The affected equipment is deployed in transportation systems across Australia and New Zealand. While fixes are available for the EB2 and VM1 models, no remediation is currently available for the ELBC2000, which is no longer sold.

title: Cisco warns of eMudhra CA compromise affecting multiple products
text:
Cisco has issued an emergency advisory after a critical compromise of eMudhra certificate authorities rendered eight intermediate certificates vulnerable to brute-force key recovery.

Between 17 and 20 October 2026, a critical security compromise involving Certificate Authorities managed by eMudhra was uncovered. A security researcher demonstrated that the private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were fundamentally broken due to an error in their Key Generation Ceremony in April 2025, allowing anyone to brute-force acquire these private keys within seconds.

Cisco has investigated its product line and identified numerous impacted devices, including IOS XE, Secure Firewall, and Identity Services Engine. For products where software fixes are available, Cisco has provided target release dates ranging from November 2026 to March 2027. Some cloud-based products, such as Duo Cloud and Meraki Dashboard, have been remediated without requiring customer action.

For products with immediate remediation steps, Cisco advises administrators to apply specific distrust guides or update trusted root lists. For example, Secure Email and Web Manager users should update to Trusted Root 2.8, while IOS XE users should follow the Cisco IOS XE and GuestShell CA Trust eMudhra Distrust Guide.

title: CISA adds four actively exploited vulnerabilities to KEV Catalog
text:
CISA has listed four new vulnerabilities in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, including critical flaws in VMware vCenter, Cisco Expressway, and Apache Roller.

CISA added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on 20 November 2026, citing evidence of active exploitation. The additions include CVE-2025-42884 in SAP NetWeaver, CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway Series, CVE-2026-123890 in VMware vCenter, and CVE-2026-129448 in Apache Roller.

The most severe issues are rated critical with a CVSS 3.1 base score of 9.8. CVE-2026-123890 is an authentication bypass in VMware Directory Service affecting vCenter versions 9.1.x, 9.0.x, 8.0, and 5.x, as well as specific Telco Cloud Platform and Infrastructure versions. CVE-2026-76466 allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root on Cisco Expressway Core and Edge devices via the database service feature.

CVE-2026-129448 in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 permits unauthenticated remote code execution through the XML-RPC endpoint, which deserializes vendor extension types before authentication. This vulnerability is identical to CVE-2026-82384 but covers a broader range of versions. CVE-2025-42884 in SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal allows unauthenticated attackers to inject JNDI environment properties, rated medium with a CVSS 3.1 score of 6.5.
